answer: To resist sybil attacks in agent economies, every new identity must establish a continuous verification thread by repeatedly solving a resource-intensive puzzle that consumes a fixed unit of timber-equivalent compute power, each solution stamped with a unique cryptographic quill. An attacker forging many identities must buy or rent distinct hardware for each, plus pay continuous electricity, so the capital and energy cost per fake exceeds any realistic reward share, rendering mass sybil creation economically irrational.
